state:
**Goal `ldap`, Stage 10 (the feature proofs) is under way.** Stages 1 to 5 and 7 to 9 are done; Stage 4 lacks only a CA a program supplies, and Stage 6 lacks only wiring the schema into the readers. `Core\Ldap`, `Core\Ldap\Filter`, `Core\Ldap\Dn`, `Core\Ldap\Sid`, `Core\Ldap\Ad` and `Core\Ldap\Change` owe nothing: every member has an `about.md`, three examples, an attack, a bench with a recorded figure in `docs/perf/members.ndjson`, and a `covers:` marker on a Rust test (and on a `.nvst` case for an instance member).

**A filter nests at most 100 levels** (`rule:core-classes/ldap-filter-is-a-value`, `nvs_ldap::MAX_FILTER_DEPTH`). A DN has no depth limit. `Filter::all` and `any` take their filters as separate arguments, so a list is passed as `...$list`.

**How proofs run with no server**, on `Core\Mail::send`'s footing: the root `nvs.toml` has an `[ldap.corp]` block at `ldaps://127.0.0.1:1`, a closed port, and one `[[app]] entry` per proof program that needs a grant. The value classes need no grant and no block: their examples print what `toString` or a reader returns. A `Change` has no reader, so its examples print `Core\Arr::count` of the list `modify` would take, or the `LogicError` message; the value's type is checked only when `modify` sends it, so `Change::replace('x', 1.5)` builds. `Connection`, `Entries`, `Entry` and `Changes` need a live connection, and no example can get one at a closed port: the user decided they run against the `samba-ad` container (see Backlog), which their proofs wait for.

The Rust side of a value class's proofs is a `// covers:` line above a test in `crates/nvs-stdlib/tests/ldap.rs` (comma-separated names are fine); an instance member also needs one in a `.nvst` case, at the end of the `--FILE--` block so no line number moves. In a proof program, a catch variable or a `var` reused in one file with another type does not compile (E0406): name each `LogicError` catch `$refusal` and each `Throwable` catch `$error`, and give every `var` in a file its own name.

items.text: **Decide how a flag reader is proved, before writing any file** (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`): `bun nv proofs --group` counts 24 features on `Core\Ldap\Ad\AccountFlags` and 9 on `Core\Ldap\Ad\GroupType`, because every readonly `bool` property is a feature. Read how `data/proofs/policy.json` treats an existing class's readonly properties (an exclusion by kind, or a skip entry per feature carrying its reason), and follow that; only `bits` and `with` are clearly members of their own. Rows at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/registry.rs:2352` and `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/registry.rs:2648`.

**`Core\Ldap\Ad\AccountFlags` and `Core\Ldap\Ad\GroupType` owe nothing**, the same proofs as `docs/examples/core/Ldap-Change/`. `crates/nvs-stdlib/tests/ldap.rs:973` (`account_flags_keep_the_bits_they_do_not_name`) and `tests/conformance/core/ldap-flag-readers-agree-with-bits.nvst` are where the `covers:` markers go. Run `nvs fmt --no-init` over the new directories before the first bless, then `bun nv proofs --run --group <class> --show --no-cache`, then `--record-perf --group <class>` in the background.

backlog: **Decided by the user: `Connection`, `Entries`, `Entry` and `Changes` prove themselves against the real `samba-ad` service** (`tests/db/compose.yaml:375`), never through a skip entry in `data/proofs/policy.json`. Three parts, before their proofs are written: (1) a marker naming the service, which makes `tools/nv/proofs/run.ts` run `docker compose up -d --wait samba-ad` before a selected program that carries it, the way `tools/nv/cmd/db-matrix.ts:346` does, and fail that program with a plain message (never skip it) when Docker is absent; programs without the marker never touch Docker. (2) a seed step that writes one fixed set of users and groups into the empty `EXAMPLE.TEST` domain, so every `.out` is stable and the examples read like a company directory. (3) the root `nvs.toml`'s `[ldap.corp]` points at the container's LDAPS port with the test CA, and the `Core\Ldap::connect` and `open` examples that print the closed-port error are rewritten to show a real sign-in.

`Ad::memberOf` with a string does not check that the string is a DN: `memberOf('not a DN')` returns `(memberOf=not a DN)`, which matches nothing (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/search.rs`, `nvs_core_ldap_ad_member_of`). `Dn::parse` on the string would throw a `LogicError` instead.

Every `Dn` member parses the slot text again (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/dn.rs`'s module doc), so walking up an n-level DN with `parent` is O(n²). A request's time limit bounds it; holding the parts instead of the text would remove it.
`nv try` does not apply an `[[app]]` grant from the root `nvs.toml`, so a probe of a granted member needs `nv proofs --bless` instead (`tools/nv/cmd/try.ts`).
Stage 4: a CA a program supplies to `Ldap::open` (`docs/agent/goals/ldap.md`).
Stage 6: wiring the schema into the readers (`crates/nvs-ldap/src/schema.rs`).
